summary: Two separate studies are stitched together as a 'cross-task' evaluation. Study I (an extension of previously published MSc work) runs five small open models (Llama 2 7B, Llama 3 8B, Gemma 2 9B, Mistral 7B, Phi-3 mini) on app-review classification: best NFR-type F1 0.55, best request-type F1 0.74. It also generates specifications from 90 reviews, scored by the first author alone. Study II runs GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-R1 once per configuration on nine Rust Project Goals to rank the top-5 Zulip messages linked to each goal or tracking issue (P@5 0.53-0.91) and to explain the links (about 4.2/5), with links validated by the authors.

claims.claim: LLM performance is strongly task-dependent and no single model consistently outperformed the others across the five RE tasks
claims.evidence: Table 15. Study I and Study II evaluate disjoint model sets on disjoint tasks, so no model is ever compared across all five tasks. The 'no single model' conclusion is an artefact of the design, not a finding.

claims.claim: Lightweight LLMs classify user feedback with moderate accuracy (NFR F1 about 0.47-0.55; request type up to 0.74)
claims.evidence: Tables 6-7 on 1,278 and 512 test reviews. Means of three runs at temperature 0 with a fixed seed (near-deterministic, no variance reported). No classical ML baseline was run; the authors only remark that results are similar to earlier ML approaches. The models are dated for 2026 (Llama 2, Phi-3 mini).

claims.claim: Lightweight LLMs produce moderate-quality specifications but fabricate requirements
claims.evidence: Table 8: mean 3.1/5 (SD 0.8), fidelity and conciseness 2-3. 90 reviews, a single rater (the first author), no reliability check, no inferential tests (conceded in §5.5).

claims.claim: Frontier LLMs identify traceability links across project artefacts with moderate-to-high performance
claims.evidence: Table 13: P@5 0.53-0.91 (best: GPT-5.5 with CoT on Issue-Zulip), NDCG@5 0.80-0.98. Nine cases, one run per configuration (72 executions). Precision only, with no recall and no ground truth. Links validated by the authors (kappa 0.83 on a 10% subset). No IR baseline (BM25/embeddings) or human-analyst comparison. The CoT effect is inconsistent (DeepSeek Issue-Zulip 0.67 -> 0.62).

claims.claim: The paper provides replication materials supporting reproducibility
claims.evidence: The references note says 'The replication package will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the manuscript'. Nothing is public at the time of the preprint, although the abstract lists it as a contribution.

patterns.note: LLM recovery of goal/issue-to-discussion links with human verification of the top 5. No recall, no baseline, nine cases. Links go from requirement to discussion, not to code.

Mining heterogeneous artefacts (app reviews, tracking issues, chat) for requirement knowledge and rationale before specifying. Feasibility numbers only, with no comparison against plain search or manual analysis.
Small LLMs drafted SRS documents from feedback that were fluent but fabricated requirements (fidelity 2-3/5); single rater, no comparison with human-written specifications.
Authors conclude human validation is required for every RE output; no gate is implemented or measured.
Traceability explanations are asserted to help design-rationale understanding and developer onboarding; this is not measured.

methodology.sample: Study I: 1,278 NFR and 512 request-type test reviews; 90 reviews for specification generation. Study II: 9 Rust Project Goal cases (80,642 Zulip messages in total), 72 single executions
methodology.baselines: Only model and prompt variants; no classical ML classifier, no IR traceability baseline, no human analyst
methodology.models: Study I: Llama 2 7B, Llama 3 8B, Gemma 2 9B, Mistral 7B, Phi-3 mini. Study II: GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-R1
methodology.variance: Study I: mean of three near-deterministic runs, no variance or tests. Study II: one run per configuration
methodology.ablations: Prompting strategies (zero-shot, few-shot, CoT, constraint, role) only
methodology.contamination_controls: Not discussed; public app-review datasets and public 2024-2026 Rust artefacts
methodology.languages: English natural-language artefacts; Rust project context in Study II

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; Study I previously published (Mallya et al.)
standards.artifacts: Replication package promised 'upon acceptance'; not public

biases.detail: Cross-task model conclusions are drawn from disjoint model sets; precision@5 without recall cannot show traceability completeness.
Nine traceability cases with single runs; specification quality judged on 90 reviews by one rater.
Replication package, the claimed contribution, is withheld until acceptance.
'Industrial case study' uses public Rust OSS artefacts, chosen because an industrial partner (Huawei) contributes to Rust; no industrial data or practitioners.
'First cross-task evaluation' is two unconnected studies, one already published, joined in a synthesis table.
No non-LLM or simple-retrieval baseline for any task.
Public datasets and public Rust discussions likely in pretraining; not addressed.

coi.affiliations: Lero / University of Limerick; Trinity College Dublin and CNR; University of Padova; The Open University
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: none; Study II done during a research visit to Huawei Ireland Research Center, with DeepSeek-R1 chosen as 'of interest to our industrial partner'
coi.detail: Industrial partner shaped model choice; no product of the authors or partner is evaluated.

verdict_reason: On-topic for pre-spec requirement discovery and traceability, but it is descriptive feasibility data with no baselines. The traceability study has nine cases, single runs and precision only; the specification rating has a single rater. The abstract's cross-task headline and replication claim are not supported by the body. Low weight.
applicability: Weakly informs a pre-spec discovery step that mines tickets, PR threads and chat across the 4+ ingestion repos. 'Rank the top-5 related discussions with an explanation, human confirms' looks feasible with frontier models (P@5 0.6-0.9 on Rust goals). But nobody measured what was missed (no recall), it was never compared with plain search, and small local models were impractical at this context length. Specification drafting from raw feedback fabricated requirements, so humans should keep authoring acceptance criteria. The paper does not address requirement-to-code links, which a spec-driven Java team needs most.

conflicts_with.detail: There, Copilot CLI's requirement-satisfaction and code-location judgments on a Java EHR codebase scored low against an expert ground truth (F1 0.381 / 0.203) while users agreed 91-94%. This paper reports 'high' traceability precision validated by its own authors without a ground truth, suggesting that author-validated precision can overstate reliability.
